Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
Comments: Angola IXP active with 14 peers, 127G total speed [PeeringDB](https://www.peeringdb.com/ix/421)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via angonix's PeeringDB record (24 peers, 330G capacity; members include Angola Cables, Angola Telecom, Unitel, ZAP, Africell) and the ISOC Pulse IXP tracker, showing an active, moderately-participated national IXP. Code unchanged; original source (ix/421, an older/duplicate PeeringDB listing) replaced with the primary angonix listing.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Available data (ITU mobile cellular subscriptions: 70.05/100 in 2023; GSMA mobile connections: 78.4% of population in Jan 2024) measure SIM subscriptions/connections, not unique subscribers as the variable requires, and connection counts overstate unique subscribers where multi-SIM ownership is common. No Angola-specific GSMA unique-subscriber percentage was found in open sources. Flagged for human review with access to GSMA Intelligence's unique subscriber dataset; code left unchanged pending that check.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
Comments: Law 22/11 enacted, Data Protection Agency established [Hunton](https://www.hunton.com/privacy-and-cybersecurity-law-blog/angola-passes-personal-data-protection-law)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: Law 22/11 (2011) established Angola's data protection framework; the Agência de Protecção de Dados (APD) was formally constituted in 2016 and has been actively enforcing it — imposing sanctions on five companies in June-July 2024 (Lexology; RVA/PLMJ). This substantiates 'legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established' (code 4). Not upgraded to 5 as evidence of AU Convention/regional alignment was not found.
